issues.display_title: Issue #793: feat(preview): route step selection — floor switch, leg focus and highlight (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-793-step-selection.mp4

Source PRD: #770 · Design: #774 · Depends on #792 (route result UI)

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Make the timeline steps selectable: pressing a step switches to its floor, focuses the map on that leg and highlights it. Pressing again, or any recalculation, returns to the whole-route view. R32-R40, plus the step-selection analytics event from PRD §8.

Nothing like this exists today — grep -rn "selectedStep|selectedLeg|stepIndex" src returns 0 hits.

Scope

Selection state

Hold it in PreviewOverlay where the map can read it, not in dirState. R38 ("selection never mutates the route") then holds by construction: dirState is only ever written through onStateChange (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:920).

Clear the selection on every recalculation — destination change, origin change, pin move, endpoint cleared (R39).

Floor switch (R33)

setActiveLevelId(id); setVisibleLevelIds(null) — the pair FloorSelector.tsx:39-44 uses, already used inside PreviewOverlay at :560-562. Respect the single-level constraint documented at PreviewOverlay.tsx:151-162 (#770 says :138-148; the block moved). Note the comment there: visibleLevelIds === null does not mean "all levels" — it resolves to the active level, which is the floor Direction operates on.

Leg highlight (R35) — not where #770 says

#770 sends this to useDirectionMapLayers. That hook draws no route line — it owns only the dropped-pin symbol layer (src/components/editor/preview/useDirectionMapLayers.ts:14-15, :79-84). The route line is stroked on the 2D label canvas: routeLines (PreviewOverlay.tsx:467-475) → useFloorPlanLabels.ts:323-343 (rgba(255,255,255,0.85) halo at width 7, rgba(59,130,246,0.9) at width 4). Putting a highlight layer in the maplibre hook would create a second rendering path fighting the canvas one. The highlight belongs in routeLines / useFloorPlanLabels.

The highlight colour must read apart from the full-route line over both light and satellite basemaps.

Camera focus (R34) — no fitBounds

#770 asks for fitBounds. It is deliberately rejected in this overlay: PreviewOverlay.tsx:316 records that it flattens the tilted 3D view. handleRecenter (:311-333) uses cameraForBounds + easeTo instead; the floor-altitude-aware variant is usePreviewSelectionLayers.ts:137-142. Follow that path.

Related gotcha: MapLibre flyTo/easeTo ignore options.elevation — set the centre elevation first, then ease.

useDirectionMapLayers already flies to activeRoutePath[0] once per distinct From, ref-guarded by lastFlownFrom (:36-49). Selection focus must not fight that one-shot.

Outdoor step (R40)

segment.levelId === null already means outdoor (multiLevelRoute.ts:30), and routeLines at PreviewOverlay.tsx:472 already draws null-level segments unconditionally. Focus the outdoor leg without forcing a floor change.

Unfocusable legs

If a leg cannot be focused, suppress the interaction rather than moving the map somewhere wrong. The step stays readable.

Analytics (PRD §8)

Add one step-selection reporter to src/lib/analytics/previewEvent.ts (four reporters live there today, :28, :59, :95, :110) and its key to the AnalyticsEvent union (src/lib/analytics/events.ts:11-50) — no route-step event exists anywhere yet. Include surface via the existing previewSurface() (previewEvent.ts:10-18, consumed at PreviewOverlay.tsx:131). Segmentation is Record<string, string | number | boolean> (events.ts:57) — flat values only, no nested objects. Do not change reportRoutePlanned or reportWayfindingOpened.

Accessibility

Selected state distinct from hover and focus. Focus ring, sane keyboard order, and a tap target usable while walking.

Tests

Recalculation clears the selection; selecting a step on another floor switches the active level; selecting the outdoor step does not change the floor; selection never writes dirState.

Out of scope

The compact layout — separate task.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-route-step-selection, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #808 -> development, stacked on #806 (#792). Branch feature/793-route-step-selection, commit 4d60668, built in a git worktree.

Three corrections to the plan above, all verified against the code first.

  1. The highlight is not in useDirectionMapLayers. That hook owns the dropped-pin symbol layer and nothing else; the route line is stroked on the 2D label canvas (useFloorPlanLabels), because a maplibre line layer has no z and would render flat on the ground under an upper-floor leg. The selected leg is a flag on routeLines, stroked amber while the rest of the route dims. Amber, not a deeper blue: it has to separate from the route it is part of, over a light basemap and over satellite.

  2. No fitBounds. It is ruled out in this overlay (PreviewOverlay.tsx:316 — it frames upright and flattens the tilted 3D view). The leg is framed with cameraForBounds for the zoom, then flown with focusPanoCamera, which sets the centre elevation first so the camera aims at the floor's altitude.

  3. Transfer steps are selectable, because the design selects one (#774 shows "Take Escalator 3 to Level 2" in the selected state). A transfer covers no ground, so every step now carries a focus target in routeSteps: a lift frames the leg it delivers the visitor to, Arrive frames the last leg.

R39 became a derivation, not an effect. useEffect(() => setSelectedStep(null), [routeResult]) is what react-hooks/set-state-in-effect refuses. The selection stores the route it was made on and is read back only while that route is current, so a recalculation drops it with nothing to run. R38 holds by construction: dirState has one writer and this is not it. (Also caught: selection/setSelection were already taken at PreviewOverlay.tsx:67.)

Analytics: directions_step_selected, segmentation { kind, position, surface }, position bucketed first/early/later so a long route does not mint a Countly value per row. Step text never leaves the browser. The existing two events are untouched.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/793/video-793-step-selection.mp4, 1920x1080 / 60 fps / 104 s, recorded against a second dev server on this branch. Renderer receipt ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312 (NVIDIA Tesla P4)). One route covers every case this project can show — developer room (wanareja, Floor 1) to atap kelapa (kelapa residence, Floor 2): the indoor leg highlights and the rest dim, the walk outside focuses without touching the floor, the last leg moves the floor selector to Floor 2, pressing again restores the whole route, and a new destination drops the selection. All asserted inside the scenario; the run logs floor after the upstairs leg: Floor 1 -> Floor 2.

Not in the video: a lift/stairs row and its floor badge — the shared demo project has no vertical connector, so a cross-floor trip inside one building fails with "No access point on this floor". Covered by unit tests.

issues.display_title: Issue #794: feat(preview): compact route layout for small screens and embedded projects (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-794-compact.mp4

Source PRD: #770 · Design: #774 · Depends on #792 (route result UI)

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

A compact route layout for small screens and embedded projects. Same information and same step order as the full layout — a change of density, not of content. R41-R46, R52.

Nothing responsive exists in this panel today: DirectionPanel.tsx:67 is a fixed max-w-[300px], and neither DirectionPanel.tsx nor PreviewOverlay.tsx contains a single sm: / md: / lg: class. There is no useMediaQuery / matchMedia hook in the codebase either — the only matchMedia call is an unrelated reduced-motion check (src/components/landing/LostRoomScene.tsx:63).

Scope

Reach the panel with the flag

embedded already exists as a PreviewOverlay prop (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:57) but currently changes exactly two things: infoCardHidden (:128, consumed :937) and the analytics surface label (:131). It is never passed to DirectionPanel. Pass it, alongside a small-viewport check.

The embedded path is src/app/embed/[key]/page.tsx:9 → LivePage embedded → src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx:75 → <PreviewOverlay live embedded={embedded} />.

Layout

  • Status and summary always rendered, never collapsed away (R42).
  • Step list collapsible, opening expanded on the first found route (R43, R44).
  • Reduced row density — same content, less padding (R46).
  • Long step lists scroll inside the route section; the panel must not grow past the viewport (R45). Specify where the scroll boundary sits and whether it fades.
  • Per-step distance stays in compact (R52). Do not design it away — it matters most on a phone, where the visitor is actually walking.
  • Check against the embedded viewer's smallest realistic viewport.

Reuse, do not build primitives

src/components/ui/ has no collapsible and no scroll-area primitive (11 files, checked). Two things already in the repo cover it:

  • Collapsible: the hand-rolled pattern at src/components/setup/import-mappedin/LocationInfoSection.tsx:20-60 — header is a real <button> with aria-expanded / aria-controls (:31-33), ChevronDown rotating (:36-41), body collapsing via CSS grid grid-rows-[1fr] → grid-rows-[0fr] + overflow-hidden (:53-58, "collapses without measuring height in JS"). It is hardcoded to --wizard-* tokens — retokenise to --editor-*, do not fork the mechanism.
  • Scrolling: the .slim-scrollbar utility, src/app/globals.css:328-351, already used by EventPanel.tsx:97 with overscroll-contain.

Tests

Compact layout renders status and summary with the step list collapsed/expanded; per-step distance still present in compact.

Notes

Design #774 is screenshots only — the compact breakpoint and the scroll boundary need to come off those, or be redlined with the designer before build.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-route-compact-layout, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #810, merged to development as cec9dbd. Branch feature/794-route-compact-layout, commit 2bbef1a (4 files, +239/-48).

R45 turned out not to be a compact-layout gap. The panel had no height bound at all: fixed chrome ~350px, step rows 52-73px, so on a 667px phone the end of the route fell off the screen — and was unreachable, because the ancestor is position: fixed with no overflow and a fixed element's overflow does not extend document scroll height. The cap is therefore unconditional, not gated on compact.

Three corrections to the plan above.

  1. Not 100dvh - --editor-topbar-h. Copying that from SearchAreaPanel / EventPanel would have cloned a defect: this overlay only insets by the topbar when standalone (PreviewOverlay.tsx:878), so it is 48px wrong on /v/[key], /embed/[key] and the editor mount. dvh also tracks a URL bar a fixed box does not follow, and equals vh inside an iframe. Used bottom-4 on the wrapper + max-h-full on the panel — a real box, no viewport unit, correct in all four mounts.
  2. Not the grid-rows-[0fr] collapse this task pointed at. That advice predates #793, which made every step a real <button> — a hidden-but-present one stays in the tab order and scrolls itself back into view on focus. The list renders conditionally instead.
  3. R44 keys on routePlanKey, not on the route object. #701 already recorded why at PreviewOverlay.tsx:481-483: the route memo depends on canvasData, so any store write — collab included — mints a fresh one and would re-open a list the visitor had just closed.

Added beyond the brief: collapsing releases a selected step (the only control that clears one is the selected row itself, so closing over it would strand a highlighted leg on the map); the panel deliberately does not take overflow-hidden, unlike both sibling panels, because the autocomplete renders its suggestions as a plain absolute child and clipping them breaks the first thing a visitor touches.

Density is CSS only — max-sm: plus a compact prop equal to embedded || tourFramed. No matchMedia: vitest.config.ts runs environment: "node" with no setupFiles, so one in the render path would take out every suite that renders PreviewOverlay.

Verified in the running app, not only in tests: 390x667 (panel 608/667), 390x480 (464/480, list scrolls 56 of 128), 1440x900 (656/900) — panel inside the viewport and status above the fold in all three. The 480px case found a real bug: flex squeezed the list to clientHeight: 0, rendering it open and empty. min-h-14 is the floor for that.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/794/video-794-compact.mp4 — 390x844, 60 fps, 98 s, ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312, Tesla P4). Recorded at phone size deliberately: the compact density is max-sm:, so a 1920x1080 recording would show none of it. Five scenes, each asserting its own measurements.

Out of scope, filed apart: at phone widths the wrapped toolbar covers the panel's "To" label — PreviewControls is z-20 with flex-wrap, the Direction wrapper sits at top-16. Measured 390x667: toolbar bottom 212 vs panel top 112, 3 buttons overlapping; clean at 1440x900. Pre-existing, and the fix belongs to the toolbar's layout.

issues.display_title: Issue #811: fix(preview): at phone widths the wrapped toolbar covers the Direction, Search and Event panels
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-811-toolbar-clearance.mp4

Found while building #794 and visible in its demo. Pre-existing — nothing in the #770 series caused it, and none of it is in the route section.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The problem

At phone widths the preview toolbar wraps to a second row and lands on top of the panel underneath it. Measured on /preview/{id} with Direction open:

viewport toolbar bottom panel top toolbar buttons overlapping the panel
390x667 212 112 3
430x932 212 112 3
768x1024 160 112 1
1440x900 108 112 none

The panel's own "To" label sits at y=125, under the wrapped row. Desktop is clean; everything at or below 768px is not.

Evidence: .playwright-mcp/demo/794/shot-iphone.png, and the #794 demo video at 390x844 shows it live.

Why

  • PreviewControls renders at absolute left-4 top-4 z-20 … flex-wrap max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] (src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx:69). It is free to wrap into the space below it, and it is a higher layer than the panels.
  • The Direction panel's wrapper is absolute … top-16 z-10 (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx), a fixed 64px offset that assumes a single toolbar row. Search and Event sit at top-20 and inherit the same assumption.
  • At 390px the toolbar has 358px to work with. "Search Area" ≈132px, "Direction" ≈114px, "Event" ≈110px, and the building and floor selectors are max-w-[11rem] each (BuildingSelector.tsx:77, FloorSelector.tsx:56) — two rows, sometimes three.
  • The editor-overlay mount is worse: PreviewControls.tsx:70 adds paddingLeft: "8.5rem" when !standalone && !live, dropping usable width to ~222px.

The wrapper is pointer-events-none with pointer-events-auto on each button, so the overlap is not merely visual — a tap that looks like it lands on the To field can open the floor dropdown instead.

Scope

The panel cannot fix this by guessing a larger top: the toolbar's height depends on how many buttons wrap, which depends on the viewport, the mount and the building and floor names. The two need to share a layout rather than both assuming.

Options worth weighing before picking one:

  1. Give the toolbar and the panels a common column — the panel starts below whatever the toolbar actually occupies, rather than at a constant.
  2. Collapse the toolbar itself at small widths (an overflow menu, or icon-only buttons — PreviewControls.tsx:80 already hides label text at sm).
  3. Move the Direction, Search and Event panels to a bottom sheet on small screens, which also resolves the second collision below.

Second collision, same cause

PreviewInfoCard is absolute right-14 top-4 z-10 w-[32rem] max-w-[calc(100vw-5rem)] (PreviewInfoCard.tsx:101). At 390px that is ~310px wide anchored near the left edge, against a Direction panel occupying x∈[16,316] — near-total overlap, and the card is later in the DOM at the same z-index, so it paints over the route result.

This is reachable by an ordinary path, not a corner case: handleSetDirections (PreviewOverlay.tsx:866-873) is the info-card's own route into Direction mode and deliberately does not clear the selection, so the card is still up when the panel opens. On desktop the two sit left and right of each other; at 390px there is no left and right.

Definition of done

  • With Direction, Search or Event open at 390x667, no toolbar control overlaps the panel, on all four mounts (editor overlay, /preview/{id}, /v/{key}, /embed/{key}).
  • Opening Direction from an Information card at 390px leaves both readable.
  • Verified in the running app at 390x667 and 430x932, not only in tests.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-mobile-overlay-layout, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #813, merged to development as 5aa7b22. Branch feature/811-mobile-overlay-layout, commit d4a91c8 (3 files, +74/-7).

Two halves, and the second is not optional.

  1. The panels follow a measured toolbar. PreviewControls reports its own height and the three wrappers use it, keeping a constant 8px gap. It cannot be a constant: the row count depends on the viewport, on the editor mount's 8.5rem left padding, and on how long the building and floor names are.
  2. The toolbar had to get smaller too. The measured offset alone was correct and useless — shipped it, ran the #794 bounds probe, and it regressed: three rows is 212px of a 667px screen, so pushing the panel below that left it no room and the "Steps" toggle went off-screen. Hiding the button labels below sm cuts it to two rows. That is the idiom already at PreviewControls.tsx:107 for "Back to Editor", and it is why each control gains an aria-label — hidden is display: none, which takes the label out of the accessibility tree with it.

Measured, toolbar bottom against panel top:

viewport before after
390x667 212 vs 112 — 3 controls overlapping 160 vs 168
430x932 212 vs 112 — 3 160 vs 168
768x1024 160 vs 112 — 1 160 vs 168
1440x900 108 vs 112 — clear 108 vs 116

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/811/video-811-toolbar-clearance.mp4 — 390x844, 60 fps, 78 s, ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312, Tesla P4). It changes the toolbar's height mid-run rather than only showing a fixed frame: Direction 160/168, Search 160/168 (identical), Overview 108/116 (the panel moves up 52px as two buttons drop), back into a building 160/168. Every scene asserts its own geometry and throws if a toolbar control lands on the panel.

Known limit, unchanged: below roughly 560px of height the panel's own chrome exceeds the space left over and its content spills past the bounded box. Everything stays reachable at 390x568, the smallest phone anyone carries.

Still open, deliberately: the PreviewInfoCard overlap described above. It is ~310px wide at 390px anchored near the left edge, against a panel at x∈[16,316], and it paints over the route result because it is later in the DOM at the same z-index. That needs a layout decision rather than a nudge, so it is left on this issue.

Needs a designer: the toolbar going icon-only below sm is a visible change no design covers — #774 is desktop only.

issues.display_title: Issue #801: fix(import): a Mappedin project is metric but reports as unscaled, so Directions hides distance (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-801-import-scale.mp4

Split out of #791 rather than folded into it: the routing library is the wrong place to fix an importer, and this needs a decision about existing projects that #791 does not.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The gap

#791 landed isScaledProject(), which decides whether a visitor may be shown a distance or a walking time. It reads realScaleMpp() — a level carrying floorplanMeta.scaleMmPerUnit that passes the 5-500 m sanity window (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts).

A Mappedin import satisfies neither, despite being genuinely metric. Its geometry is built at exactly 20 pixels per metre:
src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:11 const PIXELS_PER_METER = 20; // -> mpp = 0.05 (1px = 5cm)
src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:610 coordSpace: { cxPx: 0, cyPx: 0, mpp: 1 / PIXELS_PER_METER }
src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:573 floorplanMeta: { …, scaleMmPerUnit: null } — and only emitted at all when doors.length > 0
src/lib/mappedin-editor/convert.ts:13, :160 same 20 px/m, and no floorplanMeta written at all

So every imported project reports as unscaled and the Direction panel silently omits distance and time on it — for a source whose scale is the most trustworthy one in the product.

The stored coordSpace is not a usable substitute. StepGenerate.tsx:141 freezes computeCoordSpace() into every generated project, scale or not, so a stored mpp says nothing about whether the project was ever measured. That is exactly why isScaledProject ignores it.

Scope

  • Write the real scale on import: scaleMmPerUnit: 50 (1000 / PIXELS_PER_METER) in both converters, derived from the constant rather than typed as a literal.
  • src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:573 emits floorplanMeta only when the floor has doors. A floor with no doors then carries no scale. Decide whether to emit it unconditionally (the w: 0, h: 0 shape is already documented as "the floorplan bridge derives canvas dims from the geometry itself") or to let one scaled level speak for the project — realScaleMpp already takes the first level that has one, project-wide.
  • src/lib/mappedin-editor/convert.ts writes no floorplanMeta at all — add one, or carry the scale another way.
  • Check the sanity window before assuming this is free. With a real scale present, computeCoordSpace runs spanMeters = pxSpan × 0.05 against the 5-500 m window. A site larger than 500 m across falls back to the normalized 50 m placeholder, which would change how the model is placed on the map for such a project. Today the stored coordSpace short-circuits that path entirely, so nothing moves — confirm that still holds, or the fix ships a regression in map placement to buy a distance readout.

Existing projects

Imports already in the database keep scaleMmPerUnit: null and stay silent. Decide explicitly, do not leave it implicit:

  1. Leave them — silence is the safe failure, and a re-import fixes it.
  2. Backfill on read when a project's coordSpace.mpp came from an import.
  3. Migrate.

Option 2 needs a way to tell an imported project from a wizard-generated one, and CanvasData carries no provenance field today (checked: src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:368-401). That may be the actual prerequisite.

Tests

  • A converted Mappedin export reports isScaledProject() === true.
  • The converted project's computeCoordSpace() result is unchanged by the new field — same mpp, same centre — so map placement does not move.
  • A floor with no doors still resolves a project-wide scale.

Relates to

  • #791 — wrote isScaledProject / realScaleMpp.
  • #792 — the route summary that shows the distance this unlocks.
  • PRD #770 §11 Q2 records "a way for owners to set or correct the floor plan scale" as a follow-up need outside that PRD. This task is narrower: it does not add a control, it records a scale the importer already knows.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-mappedin-scale, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #814, merged to development. Branch feature/801-mappedin-scale, commit 068ff0c (5 files, +119/-4).

The scale is derived from PIXELS_PER_METER, not written as a literal, so the two facts cannot drift. What it unlocks: distance and estimated time in the route result, metres instead of px in the editor's wall and opening lists, and meters with real areas in the digital-twin export.

Two changes beyond the brief. floorplanMeta is now emitted for every floor of an export rather than only floors with doors — it is what carries the scale, and a doorless floor is still measured (the default test fixture is exactly that case and carried no scale at all before). The two store paths that gate on the field only map over doors, so an empty array is a no-op. And mappedin-editor/convert.ts wrote no floorplanMeta at all, so the Add-Floor import path was uncovered; it now writes one.

Placement does not move. Both converters store their own coordSpace and computeCoordSpace short-circuits on it, so the 5-500 m window never runs for an import. Asserted against the real sample export, not just a fixture.

Known limit, pinned with a test: a site wider than 500 m still reports unscaled. The window applies to every scale alike because CanvasData carries no provenance — nothing can tell an exact projection from a bad OCR read. Existing imports keep null until re-imported; no migration.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/801/video-801-import-scale.mp4, 1920x1080 / 60 fps / 143 s, GPU. It builds its own subject through the wizard and deletes it again, because the change only affects projects imported after it. Bus/Taxi Stand (Level 1) to The Atrium (Level 2): 301 m · About 5 min · 1 floor change · 4 steps, with per-step 260 m / 41 m and a Level 1 → Level 2 badge on the stairs. The scenario asserts all four and fails if the subject survives cleanup.

Incidentally the first recording anywhere of a lift/stairs step and its floor badge — the shared demo project has no vertical connector, which is why the #792 and #793 demos could only say that row was covered by tests.

issues.display_title: Issue #816: fix(map): a Closed room renders as an open box — solid mass, logo on the roof, sealed shell (#735)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-816-closed-room-roof.mp4

Source PRD: #735 · Reported from the 3D map against the reference obstruction rendering.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

#735 shipped the Closed room type: its own colour on the shell and on the walls that bound it, and a logo drawn inside its footprint. On the 3D map the result does not read as a sealed unit at all.

What ships today, and what is wrong with it:

  • The room is an open box. The area slab extrudes to area.height * wallH — the default DEFAULT_ROOM_H / WALL_H is 0.2, a fifth of the wall — so a Closed room is tall walls around a thin floor, open to the sky. The reference is one solid volume.
  • The logo is a badge, not a mark on the roof. It renders as an upright, screen-facing <img> on a frosted plate, anchored at floor height, with the room's name stacked underneath. It cannot read as printed on the room, and under pitch it sits inside the mass rather than on it.
  • The logo's box is the screen-aligned bound, so on a room turned 45° it inflates to √2 of the footprint and overhangs the walls.
  • The logo wobbles as the camera moves. The element is sized to the projected box, whose aspect changes as the roof foreshortens; object-contain re-letterboxes the image into every one of those aspects. Measured on one room across a turn and a tilt: box aspect 1.79 → 3.26, logo height 45% → 82% of the room's projected height, with the room itself unchanged. A non-affine wobble no matrix can undo.
  • Hover lights the roof only. The walls that seal the room stay unhighlighted, so a Closed room does not read as one object.
  • Its own openings are still cut into it. A boundary door (R16) leaves a notch bitten out of a shell that has no inside face, and its marker floats against the side of a solid mass.

Scope

  • Solid mass — a Closed room extrudes to just above the wall cap (closedRoomRoofOffset), clear of the cap band so the roof does not z-fight the wall strips it overlaps. Its per-room height control no longer applies: an obstruction is full height by definition.
  • Logo on the roof — anchored at closedRoomRoofHeights, and laid in the roof plane by a 2×2 recovered from the room's own projected half-axes (u = (A+B)/2 − C, v = (A−B)/2 from the two box diagonals already projected). No plate, no drop shadow, no name beside it; the selection ring moves onto the image so it shears with the roof.
  • Steady under a moving camera — the laid-out box is fixed (FIT_BASE wide, the room's plan aspect tall) and camera-independent, so object-contain fits the logo exactly once and the matrix carries scale, rotation and shear. Side effect: two fewer style writes per frame per marker.
  • Hover takes the shell — wall strips carry closedAreaId, and the 3D wall-highlight filter matches it against the same id list the area layer gets, so no caller has to know which walls belong to which room. Wall highlight paint follows the subtle hover shade.
  • Sealed shell — walls bounding a Closed room render whole: no opening cut, no window sill/header band. The marker for a boundary door goes with it.
  • Room name follows the roof — the canvas area label for a Closed room anchors at the roof, not the floor.

Acceptance

  • A Closed room on the 3D map is one solid volume in its own colour, capped at the wall top
  • Its logo is painted flat on the roof: turns, shears and scales with the surface, no plate and no name beside it
  • The laid-out logo box is identical at every camera — turning or tilting must not resize it
  • The logo box is the room's own edge, not the screen-aligned bound around it
  • Hovering a Closed room lights the roof and the walls that seal it together
  • No door or window is cut into a Closed room's shell, and no marker is left for one
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Out of scope

  • Doors on a wall shared with an ordinary room disappear for both sides. That follows the existing R9 rule (a shared wall is already painted as the Closed room's), and splitting a wall per side is its own task.
  • Logo size relative to the roof is still LOGO_PAD_RATIO = 0.5 of the largest inscribed rectangle, which on an irregular room is a small share of the footprint. A separate call if it should fill more.

RESULT

Merged to development via #817 — merge commit f0adf38, work commit ab40950.

Root cause, per symptom

  • Open box — geojson-utils extruded an area slab to area.height * wallH, and DEFAULT_ROOM_H / WALL_H = 0.2. A Closed room got the same fifth-of-a-wall slab every other room does.
  • Badge, not a mark — the marker overlay drew the logo as an upright screen-facing <img> on the button's frosted plate, anchored at levelBaseHeights (the floor), with the room name stacked under it.
  • Box inflated on a turn — the overlay projected the two box diagonals and took the screen-axis-aligned bound, which is √2 the footprint at 45°.
  • Wobble under a moving camera — the element was sized to the projected box. Its aspect changes as the roof foreshortens, and object-contain is non-linear in aspect, so the logo was re-letterboxed on every frame. Measured on one room: box aspect 1.79 → 3.26 across a turn and a tilt, logo height 45% → 82% of the room's projected height, room unchanged. No matrix could undo it — the damage happened before the matrix applied.
  • Hover missed the walls — highlightWall3d filters on wallId, and an area id matches no wall.
  • Openings still cut — wallOpenings ran on every wall, including the ones sealing a Closed room, and computeMarkerAnchors emitted a marker for the boundary door.

Fix

File Change
lib/map/geojson-utils.ts closedRoomRoofOffset / closedRoomRoofHeights; Closed rooms extrude to the wall cap; bounding walls render whole and carry closedAreaId
components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx logo anchored at the roof and laid in the roof plane by --fit-m; fixed camera-independent box (FIT_BASE, plan aspect); plate/shadow/name dropped; ring on the image; every marker on a Closed room lifted to the roof
lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts wall highlight also matches closedAreaId; wall highlight paint follows the subtle hover shade
lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/closedRoom.ts closedWallOwners (one scan, closedWallColors derives from it) and boundaryClosedArea
lib/map/object-markers.ts no marker for a door on a Closed room's own boundary
lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts a Closed room's name label anchors at the roof

Verified — pnpm test 188 files / 1677 tests, pnpm lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean. New unit tests: roof height and colour, sealed shell + closedAreaId, dropped boundary-door marker, and the logo box byte-identical across a 45° turn of both the camera and the floor.

Demo — .playwright-mcp/demo/closed-room-roof/ (1920×1080, 60 fps, 219 s). Builds the room on camera and reads its own numbers off the screen: room's square 1% → 98% mass, markers 14 → 9, hovered room + wall band 87% → 0% mass, laid-out box 512×279 at all three cameras, logo span 112 px against a 126 px screen-aligned bound after a 27° turn, 96% of the logo's square still roof with the camera tilted right over.

Left open (called out in the PR): a door on a wall shared with an ordinary room now disappears for both sides, following the existing R9 rule; and LOGO_PAD_RATIO = 0.5 still makes the logo a small share of an irregular room's footprint.
